target.name: Clippership
target.founder: Nico Cymbalist, Luca Cymbalist, Kai Matsuka

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $5M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Clippership is a Seed-stage ocean and maritime technology company that has raised $5M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a private comparables set of three peers operating in the same sector—Standard Subsea, NetworkOcean, and Albacore—given the absence of directly comparable public companies in this specialized domain.

The stage-progression method, the sole applicable triangulation approach given limited market data, applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A progression. Applied to the $5M raised proxy, this method yields an implied valuation of $12M. The triangulated range derived from this methodology spans $11M (low) to $14M (high), with $12M as the median point. This relatively tight band reflects reliance on a single analytical method and the multiplier assumptions embedded in stage-level step-up conventions.

The primary source of uncertainty is methodological: with only one applicable valuation approach and a private comparables set of three companies, the analysis lacks the granularity afforded by multi-method triangulation or liquid public market anchors. The valuation range of $11M–$14M is defensible on stage and capital-raised metrics alone, but refinement would require either additional private transaction data or progress toward near-term fundraising milestones that would calibrate the step-up assumption.
